head: mhw decides their flags
why: `mhw` with no argument prints the whole usage text, which was workstation.py's docstring. Its closing paragraph said that 'this file' decides the installers' flags; the file is gone, so the Node text says 'mhw'. The usage paragraph `mhw --help` prints is word for word the same (steps 0 to 2 are compared unchanged).

head: node: modules only, Node 26 or later \(engines\.node\)\.
why: The same text's last paragraph named the runtime: 'Standard library only, Python 3.9+.' was true of workstation.py and is false of the Node command, which imports node: modules only and needs the node engines.node names.

 {3}\])
replace: "<the sh that renders the admin stage>",
why: A hardening (test/lifecycle/admin-line.test.js only): workstation.py ran the owner-side render of install-managed.sh, and every install.sh step, as ["sh", script], so the first sh on PATH ran them; the Node commands run /bin/sh by absolute path, as mhw check already does (src/commands/check.js), so no PATH entry decides which shell runs the installers. The root command line itself (the sudo call and its arguments) is unchanged and compared.

pinned_by.test: live: in a real terminal, RETURN installs and another key aborts (Issue #113)

why: A residual, not seen in any transcript (no case has a terminal): the RETURN prompt sets `stty -icanon -echo -isig` for its one key, so Ctrl+C is 'any other key': it aborts with exit 1 and the terminal modes are restored. workstation.py kept signals on (tty.setcbreak), so Ctrl+C raised KeyboardInterrupt, a traceback. The pty arm sends \x03 and expects exit 1 with nothing written.

pinned_by.test: update without git on PATH refuses with a line, before anything runs

why: A residual, not seen in any transcript (every case has git on PATH): `mhw update` in a checkout with no git on PATH prints `REFUSE  git was not found on PATH; update needs it` and exits 2. workstation.py ran ["git", ...] and stopped with FileNotFoundError, a traceback. git is looked up through src/lib/onpath.js, absolute PATH entries only.

pinned_by.test: golden: the Node lifecycle commands match the transcripts of workstation.py

why: A residual the transcript cannot tell apart: after a checkout, workstation.py installed with the release's global/workstation.py, or ran install.sh when there was none. A release with src/commands/install.js (this one and later) has no workstation.py, so the Node command runs its bin/mhw.js install with the node running mhw; a Python release still runs its workstation.py with python3 from PATH, an older one install.sh. The checkout-update case's head side takes the Node branch (its clone has no workstation.py) and prints the same conversation the original did.

pinned_by.test: golden: the Node lifecycle commands match the transcripts of workstation.py

why: A residual in the entry point, not in what it does: in an npm install, after npm succeeds, workstation.py ran ["/bin/sh", "<package>/mhw", "install", ...flags]; the Node command runs [process.execPath, "<package>/bin/mhw.js", "install", ...flags]. The installer-argv-package case pins what that install hands install.sh and install-managed.sh (argv, overlay, MHW_NODE, MHW_CMD=mhw), the same on both sides. The new ./mhw keeps a sh line so an earlier release's /bin/sh <package>/mhw still works (test/lifecycle/npm-package.test.js).

head: (?<=^|\n)install-user \[
why: #503 (S25 of #470) moved global/install.sh to `mhw install-user` (src/commands/install-user.js): mhw install, update and uninstall now run the user layer as `<node> <package>/bin/mhw.js install-user <flags>` on the node running mhw, where they ran `/bin/sh <package>/global/install.sh <flags>`. Its recording stand-in (test/lifecycle/stub-installers.js) now replaces src/commands/install-user.js and logs the same line under that name. Every flag, its order, the managed root and the environment the installer gets (WORKSTATION_OVERLAY, MHW_NODE, MHW_CMD, WORKSTATION_MANAGED_ROOT) are unchanged and still compared; only the program's name in the log differs. The end-to-end parity of the installer itself is test/install/install-user-golden.test.js.

head: (?<=^|\n)install-admin \[
why: #496 (S26 of #470) moved global/install-managed.sh to `mhw install-admin` (src/commands/install-admin.js): mhw install, update and uninstall now run the admin layer on this process's own node and bin/mhw.js, by absolute path, where they ran /bin/sh on the script. Its stand-in (test/lifecycle/stub-installers.js) logs the same line under the new name: the same arguments (--root, --apply, --sha256, --check, --remove), in the same order, and the same environment. head: run mhw install-user as yourself to restore the user-level ones
replace: run <the user-layer installer> as yourself to restore the user-level ones
why: #496 (S26 of #470): the admin layer's --remove ended with 'run install.sh as yourself to restore the user-level ones', a pointer to a file #503 had already deleted. `mhw install-admin --remove` names `mhw install-user`, the user-layer installer since #503. The rest of the line, and of every transcript, is compared unchanged.

base: "(?:<the sh that renders the admin stage>|/bin/sh)",\n +"<INSTALL_MANAGED>"
head: "<NODE>",\n +"<MHW_JS>",\n +"install-admin"
why: #496 (S26 of #470) moved global/install-managed.sh to `mhw install-admin`: the owner-side render and the one root command now run this process's own node on this package's bin/mhw.js with the subcommand install-admin, by absolute path, where they ran /bin/sh on the script. The sudo call around it is unchanged: /usr/bin/sudo -k -p 'Password for %u: ', then the program, then --apply=STAGE --sha256=HEX (or --remove), then --root under WORKSTATION_MANAGED_ROOT, and no sudo at all there. The quoting of a stage path with a space is unchanged; the new form is spelled out in the golden test.

It named install-managed.sh, which this slice deletes; it now names install-admin (`mhw install-admin`), which is what sudo runs. The rest of the paragraph is compared unchanged.
